label: Speed varies as the square root of linear size in swimming, flight and walking
statement_en: Leaving aside differences in mechanical construction, swimming (Froude's law), flight (minimum stable speed) and walking (the leg swinging as a pendulum) all give the same result: an animal's velocity tends to vary as the square root of its linear dimensions.

hypotheses.name: thompson1917-ch02-10#assumed-1
hypotheses.statement: That the compared animals move at equal Froude number, or fly at v_min with the same ρ and C_L,max.

hypotheses.name: thompson1917-ch02-10#assumed-2
hypotheses.statement: The walking route (the leg as a pendulum) is not formalised.

scope.basis: a theorem about a model: it applies wherever the design supplies the quantities it uses and accepts the hypotheses in scope.assumed
kernelChecked: Flight: v_min(L2)/v_min(L1) = sqrt(L2/L1) under R1, R2, constant ρ and C_L,max (vmin_ratio).
Swimming: at equal Froude number v = sqrt(Fr g L), so v(L2)/v(L1) = sqrt(L2/L1) (froude_ratio).
assumed: That the compared animals move at equal Froude number, or fly at v_min with the same ρ and C_L,max.
The walking route (the leg as a pendulum) is not formalised.

C9c.basis: evaluated against one reference specimen (Cypselurus hiraii, Park and Choi 2010 Table 1 model L3); an isometric family is one body plan, so other clades are out of scope
